headlines.title: What Does Apple’s Run Mean for a 72-Year-Old Widow With $600,000 of a $1.6 Million IRA in the Stock?
headlines.summary: Apple's surge just inflated her IRA right before withdrawals become mandatory. One date at year-end locks in her first RMD, and the stock she inherited could decide how much Medicare and the IRS take from her.

headlines.title: Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Premium Income (GPIX) Adds Alphabet and Apple on Nov. 11
headlines.summary: The fund bought $86.9 million of stock and sold nothing, lifting 117 positions.

headlines.title: SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 Growth (SPYG) Buys $11.2 Million More NVDA on Nov. 11
headlines.summary: The fund added $92.9 million in net new positions, led by a $11.2 million purchase of NVIDIA, with all 152 positions increased and none decreased.

headlines.title: Proshares Trust (TQQQ) Sells $16.3 Million of Apple on Wednesday
headlines.summary: The 3x leveraged Nasdaq-100 fund cut all 100 of its positions on Wednesday, selling $192.1 million of stock and buying nothing.

headlines.title: iShares MSCI ACWI (ACWI) Adds Apple and Nvidia on Nov. 11
headlines.summary: The $32.70 billion fund bought $239.0 million in stocks, increasing 549 positions and trimming none.

description: Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; Mac, a line of personal computers; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and wearables, home, and accessories, including Apple Watch, AirPods, Beats products, Apple Vision Pro, Apple TV 4K, HomePod, and Apple HomeView, as well as Apple branded and third-party accessories. It also provides advertising services comprising third-party licensing arrangements and own advertising platforms; AppleCare and cloud services; and payment services, including Apple Card and Apple Pay. In addition, the company operates App Store that allow customers to discover and download applications and digital content, such as books, music, video, games, and podcasts. Further, it provides digital content through subscription-based services, including Apple Arcade, a game service; Apple Fitness+, a personalized fitness service; Apple Music, which offers users a curated listening experience; Apple News+, a news and magazine service; and Apple TV, which offers original content and live sports. The company sells its products and resells third-party products through its retail and online stores, and direct sales force; its services through its various service platforms; and third-party cellular network carriers and other resellers. It serves consumer, small and mid-sized business, education, enterprise, and government markets. The company operates in North and South America, European countries, India, the Middle East, Africa, China mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, and rest of Asia. The company was formerly known as Apple Computer, Inc. and changed its name to Apple Inc. in January 2007. Apple Inc. was founded in 1976 and is headquartered in Cupertino, California.
